title: Genie Agents — Meridian Financial Group lab
description: Meridian Financial Group: a synthetic US bank — transactions, reversals, a daily loan book, credit applications and fraud cases across 2.1M customers and 340 branches, over two fiscal years. The lab dataset for the Genie Agents course.

small.description: 20M transactions. Enough for everything except the performance work.

large.description: 900M transactions. Only for the performance module, where query time has to be measurable.

notebooks.name: 01_catalog_and_schemas
notebooks.title: 01 · Catalog and schemas
notebooks.intro:
Creates the schemas and the documents volume for the Meridian lab.

The first cell shows which catalog you are working in. Check it before running 02 — everything else lands there.

notebooks.name: 02_dimensions
notebooks.title: 02 · Dimensions
notebooks.intro:
Six dimensions: dates, branches, products, customers, accounts and FX rates.

Every value derives from `hash()` of the row key rather than `rand()`, and ages anchor to a fixed date rather than today. Your data is therefore byte-identical to everyone else's, which is what lets the benchmarks later in the course compare against a known answer.

notebooks.name: 03_facts
notebooks.title: 03 · Facts
notebooks.intro:
Five fact tables: transactions, reversals, the daily loan book, credit applications and fraud cases.

**This is the slow one** — it generates {{TXN_COUNT}} transactions plus roughly 35M daily loan-balance snapshots. Expect several minutes on a small warehouse, longer if it is cold.

Read the row counts it prints at the end. You will be asked about them.

notebooks.name: 04_staging
notebooks.title: 04 · Staging
notebooks.intro:
Two objects that exist in most real lakehouses and that nobody has cleaned up: a very wide raw landing table, and a superseded revenue table still sitting next to its replacement.

They are here because deciding what *not* to point an agent at is part of the job.

notebooks.name: 05_governance
notebooks.title: 05 · Governance
notebooks.intro:
Row-level and column-level access control, plus certification tags.

**Needs privilege** to create functions and ALTER the tables, and the `mfg_*` account groups to exist. If you cannot run it, skip it — everything else still works.

notebooks.name: 06_curated
notebooks.title: 06 · Curated layer
notebooks.intro:
The objects an agent should actually be pointed at: net-revenue and month-end views, a customer view without identifiers, and three Unity Catalog functions.

**Attempt the curation exercise before running this.** It is the worked answer — opening it first turns an exercise into a reading task.

notebooks.name: 07_metric_view
notebooks.title: 07 · Metric view
notebooks.intro:
One definition of each headline metric, declared once and correct however it is grouped at query time.

Defining "net fee revenue" separately in five places is how five teams end up with five numbers.

notebooks.name: 99_validate
notebooks.title: 99 · Validate
notebooks.intro:
Twelve checks confirming the dataset is complete and behaving as expected. Every row should read PASS.

Read the numbers, not just the verdicts — several of them are the point.
